title: Powernode Module Manifest
description: Authoritative schema for extensions/system/modules/*/manifest.yaml and extensions/system/templates/{module-repo,example-modules}/*/manifest.yaml. See docs/MODULE_MANIFEST_COMPLETE_SCHEMA.md for prose reference.

schema_version.description: Schema version. Only v1 is supported today.

name.description: Stable identifier. Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; must start with a letter and not end in a hyphen.

category.description: Platform layering taxonomy slug (System::NodeModuleCategory::PLATFORM_TAXONOMY) — determines this module's position in the overlay union stack (bottom = base layers, top = application layers). Optional: modules without one fall back to the seed's default 'workloads' bucket. See db/seeds/powernode_platform_categories.rb.

carve_waivers.description: Build-tooling-only (not yet a NodeModule DB column — read directly from the YAML by scripts/module-build/derive-file-spec.sh, so an unrecognized key here still round-trips through ManifestImportService's manifest_extras forward-compat path). Globs of paths this module's package_spec owns (per dpkg -L) but deliberately does NOT carve into file_spec — silences derive-file-spec.sh's conformance under-carve WARN for the matched paths. See docs/MODULE_MANIFEST_COMPLETE_SCHEMA.md's Content specs section.

items.description: A module this one requires. Two forms: a name pin '<owner>/<module>@<version-constraint>' (e.g. 'powernode/powernode-base-ruby@^1.0'), or a capability requirement 'capability:<tag>[@<constraint>]' (e.g. 'capability:os.userland', 'capability:database.postgres@>= 16'). A capability constraint is matched at import with Gem::Requirement, so it must use Gem syntax ('>= 16', '~> 1.0', '1.0') — npm caret ('^16') is NOT valid there, even though name pins conventionally use it. The runtime authority is System::CapabilityResolver.constraint_valid?; this pattern is the PR-time mirror of that rule and must stay consistent with it.

anyOf.title: Name pin
anyOf.description: '<owner>/<module>@<constraint>' or a bare module name. The constraint is recorded but never parsed — the platform has no module semver (NodeModuleVersion#version_number is an integer counter) — so caret syntax is accepted here.

anyOf.title: Capability requirement
anyOf.description: 'capability:<tag>[@<Gem::Requirement constraint>]'. Rejects caret and other non-Gem syntax, which would otherwise fail to parse at import and surface to the operator as a MISSING PROVIDER rather than as the manifest typo it is.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the service. Values are forwarded to systemd which interprets them as strings; YAML scalar values of any type are accepted here.

unit_body.description: Verbatim systemd unit body; the agent renders it through the same write/enable/detach lifecycle as a generated unit (see MODULE_MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md). Mutually exclusive with start_command (enforced server-side).

dependencies.description: Per-service ordering: this service starts after the named sibling services (rendered as After=/Requires= on the generated powernode-<module-id>-<name> unit).

users.description: Fleet-managed Unix users this module needs. The agent's etcidentity unions these across installed modules to render /etc/passwd + /etc/shadow. uid/primary_gid are allocated by the platform (reserved.go) and may be absent in the authored manifest.

groups.description: Fleet-managed Unix groups this module needs (rendered into /etc/group). gid is platform-allocated and may be absent in the authored manifest.

sudoers.description: Sudo grants this module declares. The agent's etcsudoers validates each via visudo -cf and writes one /etc/sudoers.d/powernode-<module>-<id> file per grant. `runas` is the authored alias the platform maps to runas_user.

skills.description: AI Skills this module ships. Each entry is an object whose schema is owned by the skill subsystem; this manifest only validates that it's an array.

gitleaks_version.description: Pinned gitleaks release fetched as a sha256-verified binary (gitleaks module). Bump alongside the pinned amd64 (x64) / arm64 checksums in the gitleaks case of scripts/module-build/stage15.sh.

gh_version.description: Pinned GitHub CLI (gh) release fetched as a sha256-verified binary (gh module). Bump alongside the pinned amd64 / arm64 checksums in the gh case of scripts/module-build/stage15.sh; values come from the release's gh_<ver>_checksums.txt.

go_version.description: Pinned Go toolchain version (runtime-go module). Bump alongside the per-arch tarball checksums in the runtime-go case of scripts/module-build/stage15.sh.

claude_code_version.description: Pinned Claude Code CLI version installed by the claude-tmux module (read at scripts/module-build/stage15.sh's claude-tmux case). The script's jq fallback silently unpins when this key is absent — declare it here rather than deleting it from a manifest.

grok_version.description: Pinned Grok Build CLI (@xai-official/grok) version npm-installed by the grok-cli module (read at scripts/module-build/stage15.sh's grok-cli case). Same reproducibility unit as claude_code_version — an npm package has no single release-binary sha256, so the exact version plus npm's own integrity metadata IS the pin. The script's jq fallback silently unpins when this key is absent — declare it here rather than deleting it from a manifest.

ubuntu_digest.description: Pinned Ubuntu base image digest. Format: sha256:<64-hex>, or null to inherit Containerfile default.

apt_snapshot.description: Pinned snapshot.ubuntu.com APT snapshot timestamp, consumed by build-platform-modules.yaml Stage 1 as the mmdebstrap base_url (campaign 019f5885 inc5 — determinism hardening). Format: YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ. Null (field omitted) and the literal string "none" are equivalent documented opt-outs — both fall back to the live archive.ubuntu.com mirror (today's behavior), for a module whose exact package set snapshot.ubuntu.com hasn't caught up on yet.

ruby_version.description: Pinned Ruby version to source-compile (runtime-ruby module). Keep in sync with server/.ruby-version.

node_version.description: Pinned Node.js version to fetch as a prebuilt linux-x64 binary (runtime-node module). Keep in sync with frontend/.nvmrc.

act_runner_version.description: Pinned Gitea act_runner version fetched as a sha256-verified linux-amd64 binary (gitea-act-runner module). Bump alongside the pinned checksum(s) in build-platform-modules.yaml Stage 1.5.

vault_version.description: Pinned HashiCorp Vault release for the `vault` module. Bump alongside the per-arch sha256 pair in the `vault` case of scripts/module-build/stage15.sh — the checksums are per-version AND per-arch, and a version bump without them fails the build closed.

restart_after_update.description: Declares that updating THIS module requires restarting ANOTHER module's service — for a module whose own `services` block is empty, updating it otherwise restarts nothing and the new code sits on disk unloaded. Fires on the heartbeat that reports this module's new digest materialised, not at promotion. Mirrors System::ModuleConfigValidator.validate_restart_after_update; see System::RestartAfterUpdate.

module.description: NAME of the module whose service must restart.

services.description: Service names within that module. Note the plural — a singular `service:` key is ignored by the importer and would silently restart nothing, which is the inert-deploy failure this block exists to remove.

verify.description: IMP-3855ff9908f2 — post-deploy self-proof. Each probe asserts that a BARE command name resolves, through PATH, to exactly the declared path. `resolves_to` is REQUIRED: an existence check is what passed while the VM-9000 binary was shadowed. There is deliberately no `shells` key — every probe runs in BOTH a login and a non-login shell, because the divergence between the two IS the bug class. See docs/MODULE_MANIFEST_COMPLETE_SCHEMA.md and System::ModuleVerify.

name.description: Identifier; concatenated into the signal fingerprint a failed probe raises.

command.description: BARE command name — no slash, no shell metacharacter. An absolute path would resolve itself instead of exercising the PATH lookup, so it could never detect a shadowing binary.

resolves_to.description: REQUIRED absolute canonical path the command must resolve to in BOTH shells.
